name: Sandstone
lede: Sandstone is a muted yellow-tan named for the rock, and the books that define the word do not agree on its shade.

sections.title: A rock's name
sections.body: *Sandstone* names the sedimentary rock, and the color word follows the rock [1]. ColorHub's library carries it from two color lists, the xkcd survey and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, where it is block 42; the older Maerz & Paul dictionary of 1930 records it as first used in 1902 [2]. The same lists file the swatch under two other names, Light French Beige and Very Light Brown [2].

sections.title: Books disagree on the shade
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines sandstone as a reddish brown [1]. The same dictionary defines *freestone-coloured*, a term Shakespeare used in *As You Like It*, as an orangey-yellow, the color of limestone or sandstone [1]. The swatch here sits nearer the second reading, a yellowish tan rather than a red brown [2].

A rock name covers whatever the rock happens to be. The Pigment Compendium notes sandstones that carry grains of green glauconite [3] and others cemented with baryte [4], so the stone is not one color, and no single swatch can stand for all of it.

sections.title: The rock in the books
sections.body: The color books mostly meet sandstone as a place. Finlay describes an underground home dug into it, its walls flecked with a natural pink pattern that looked like marbled paint [5]. In the same chapter an opal mine's walls carry the marks of a jackhammer used to test the sandstone for opal [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the library the swatch reads lightness 72, chroma 33 and hue 87 in LCH, and its nearest named neighbor is [[tan]], a distance of 5.5 in ΔE [2]. Nearby names are [[khaki]] and [[sand]], and Paterson separately defines *sandy* as the color of sand [1]. Screen colors are approximate.

questions.q: How does Paterson's dictionary define sandstone as a color?
True or false: a rock name such as sandstone points to one exact shade.

openers: Two books define sandstone two ways: one says reddish brown, the other treats it as an orangey-yellow stone color.
